subject: Request: Tail-latency carveout for Dedicated pool — Quantumpay
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@quantumpay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, contracts@quantumpay.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated SLA request: tail latency for fraud model

Hi Rachel,

We're getting close to final sign-off on the Quantumpay integration. The payments fraud team has one outstanding ask: a carveout in the Dedicated SLA around tail latency (99.9th percentile) for our fraud scoring model. This model is latency-sensitive — spikes in tail latency directly translate to customer declines.

Can Redwood provide a documented exception that guarantees 99.9p latency <= 350ms for dedicated GPUs serving qp-fraud v2 (seq len ~512), or alternatively offer a documented mitigation plan (reserved concurrency + preemptible warm nodes + fallback to quantized variant) if you cannot meet the hard guarantee? We need language to show procurement/legal.

I've attached our internal SLA sensitivity analysis (qpay_sla_analysis.pdf).

Thanks,
Alex Reed
Sr. PM, Risk & Fraud
Quantumpay

Attachments: qpay_sla_analysis.pdf (pdf)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@quantumpay.com>

Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA request: tail latency for fraud model

Alex — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment.

High level: we can offer a contractual carveout for the Quantumpay Dedicated pool but need to align on measurable conditions (traffic patterns, SLO window, and allowed mitigation). I've looped in Neha (infra) and Marcus (solutions) to confirm technical feasibility and a recommended SLA clause; Laura from legal to scope the contract language.

Proposed next steps:
- Neha to confirm achievable 99.9p numbers for qp-fraud v2 on a dedicated 8xA100 pool with your expected qps profile.
- Marcus to propose a fallback plan (reserved concurrency + pre-warmed nodes + a quantized fallback) and estimated cost delta.
- Laura to draft a short carveout paragraph we can insert into the MSA (2–3 sentences) + a timeline for sign-off.

Can you also share a week of production P95/P99 histograms and expected peak qps? That will let us validate headroom. We're happy to run a short canary once we have traffic shape.

I'll attach a draft service matrix showing where carveouts live vs standard SLA.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment.

Alex — quick technical note from infra:

Summary of feasibility (given Quantumpay inputs provided so far):
- Baseline: qp-fraud v2 (seq len ~512) on 8xA100 dedicated pool can achieve median token latency ~20ms; P99.9 latency is workload-sensitive and driven by burstiness and KV cache warmup.
- Recommended contractual carveout approach:
  1) Guaranteed P99.9 <= 350ms when customer subscribes to a reserved concurrency of >= 120 concurrent requests and a minimum pool headroom of 25% (we reserve extra' nodes to absorb bursts).
  2) If headroom thresholds are exceeded, Redwood will execute a documented mitigation: (a) traffic shaping to reserved concurrency, (b) immediate spin-up of hot-warm prewarmed nodes (expected ramp: 90–180s), (c) failover to a quantized v2-q variant with degraded but bounded quality.
  3) Monitoring: 1s sampling of tail latency metrics and automated paging to both Quantumpay on-call and Redwood SRE when 2 consecutive 1-min windows breach P99.9 bound.
- Cost/ops impact: estimated 8–12% uplift on monthly committed spend for the additional headroom and warm-node reservation. Marcus will provide a detailed estimate.

If that aligns with Quantumpay's risk tolerance, we can produce a short clause for contracts and a runbook for the mitigation steps. Also recommend a 2-week canary (traffic mirrored) before cutover.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
